newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan Brady debt buyback fund nears approval.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan Brady debt buyback fund nears approval.

text.p: Venezuelan plans to set up a Debt Rescue Fund that would be used to pay down foreign and domestic debt with windfall oil revenues neared completion Wednesday as the Senate approved it during a second reading, legislators said.
The bill now goes to Congress for a final reading where passage is expected to take around two weeks.

Once approved, the fund will be discreetly administered by the Venezuelan Investment Fund, buying back debt "at those moments most appropriate for the public interest," said Senator Haydee Castillo of opposition social democrat party Copei.

"The important part is to buy back principal, as that relieves our debt service burden in future years," Castillo said, adding that the law allowed for the purchase of up to 25 percent of total Venezuelan internal and external debt.
Venezuelan Brady prices have firmed in recent months on the possibility of Venezuelan buybacks, analysts say.
